paper.title_en: Constraining invisible neutrino decay at NO$\nu $A and DUNE
paper.abstract_en:
The main emphasis of this study is to explore the relevance of invisible neutrino decay within the frameworks of both the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE) and the NuMI off-axis $
u _{e}$ appearance (NO$
u $A) experiments. Under the normal mass hierarchy, we suppose that $
u _3$ is unstable and will eventually decay into a sterile state. In this work, we have studied the potential of these combinations to constrain the decay parameter. We have observed that the true value of $	heta _{23}$ can significantly affect the constraint on the decay parameter. A true value of $	heta _{23}$ in the HO can significantly improve the constraint. At the HO, for ${	au _3}/{m_3}=2	imes 10^{-11}$ s/eV, DUNE and the combination of DUNE and NO$
u $A can rule out the no decay scenario at 3$\sigma $ CL. For the given ${	au _3}/{m_3}$, DUNE and the combination can measure ${	au _3}/{m_3}$ at 3$\sigma $, in the range [$7.22	imes 10^{-11}>{	au _3}/{m_3}> 1.16	imes 10^{-11}$] s/eV and [$6.10	imes 10^{-11}>	au _{3}/m_{3}>1.19	imes 10^{-11}$] s/eV, respectively. This precision measurement of ${	au _3}/{m_3}$ improves significantly for the value of $	heta _{23}$ in the HO compared to the lower octant (LO). Our analysis also yields measurements of CP sensitivity for DUNE, NO$
u $A, and DUNE+NO$
u $A in the context of invisible neutrino decay. In this work, we consider three values of the decay parameter to illustrate the analysis.
